properties.title: Tornado Warning issued October 10 at 6:01PM EDT until October 10 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:

or 16 miles northeast of Aiken, moving north at 30 mph.

to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

and 36.

outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to an interior room
or closet on the lowest floor of a sturdy building immediately.

properties.title: Tropical Storm Watch issued October 10 at 1:54PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Julian
- Pine Valley

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 25-35 mph with gusts to 50 mph

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 39
to 57 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for hazardous wind of equivalent tropical storm
force.

completed as soon as possible. Prepare for limited wind
damage.

are shallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley
locations that don't typically experience strong winds.
Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within
urban or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving
conditions on bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional 1-3 inches, with locally
higher amounts

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for major
flooding rain

the previous assessment.

major flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues are
likely.
- PREPARE: Strongly consider protective actions, especially
if you are in an area vulnerable to flooding.

action will likely result in serious injury or loss of life.

- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and
rescues.

multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos,
and ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides.
Flood control systems and barriers may become stressed.

communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or
washed away. Many places where flood waters may cover
escape routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of
moving water with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions
become dangerous. Many road and bridge closures with some
weakened or washed out.

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Tornadoes not expected
- The tornado threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Tornadoes are not expected. Showers and thunderstorms
with gusty winds may still occur.
- PREPARE: Little to no preparations needed to protect

- ACT: Listen for changes in the forecast.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 2:03PM EDT until October 13 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in South
Carolina...North Carolina...

(English) Broad River Near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W Blacksburg
affecting Cleveland and Cherokee Counties.

.Heavy tropical showers will continue to overspread the Broad River
basin through tonight with 3 or 4 inches of rain accumulating.
Excessive runoff remains likely to develop pushing the river out of
it's banks on Sunday.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W
Blacksburg.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues. At this
level, minor flooding of low-lying farmland along the river may be
ongoing. Areas along Buffalo Breek may be beginning to flood due to
backwater effects. At 15.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.
The Broad River may be approaching River Rd. and Little Hope Rd.
near US 29.  Adjacent farmland and low-lying area flooding is
continuing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.7 feet and rising slowly.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.9 feet
Monday morning with a reasonable worse case scenario of near 18
feet.
